title: Affordable recreation before variety upgrades
applies_when: Recreation alerts, boredom or an approved recreation objective need assessment.
approach: Treat a variety alert as evidence to assess, not a checklist to clear immediately. Check actual recreation need, boredom, expectations and usable existing options before proposing additional kinds.
For an early camp, prefer one modest usable option that can be built with current accessible supplies. A horseshoe pin is an example to compare, not a required definition or universal choice.

Compare the complete native cost: fixed ingredients as well as the chosen building material, construction labor and usable space. If an option requires unavailable ingredients, choose a feasible alternative or defer it with an explicit supply dependency.
Before optional variety upgrades, consider unfinished shelter, food and storage work and the available construction labor. Keep a larger future facility in the future plan until it is justified.
Provide time and access to use recreation. Another copy of the same kind does not solve a need for a different kind.
verify: Usable recreation cells, time available, actual thoughts and changes in needs.
reconsider: Pain, grief or an individual requirement is the main cause; furniture may not resolve it.
